approval_time_estimate: 1–4 weeks (product approval; LinkedIn publishes no timeline)
summary: LinkedIn OAuth has a unique tiered API product access model. Basic OAuth for sign-in works easily, but any meaningful data access (posting, reading connections, company data) requires applying for specific 'Products' within LinkedIn's Developer Portal — each with its own approval process taking 1–4 weeks. LinkedIn is one of the most restrictive platforms: many API capabilities are available only to Marketing Partners or require specific use-case justification.
key_facts: Basic OAuth (sign in with LinkedIn, read basic profile) is self-service
Any advanced access (posting, reading connections, company pages) requires Product approval
LinkedIn's approval is use-case based — they want to know specifically what you're building
Marketing API and company data requires LinkedIn Marketing Partner status (very restrictive)
LinkedIn is listed as Composio-managed OAuth — good for prototyping; you still need your own app for production
Rate limits on LinkedIn APIs are very strict even with approval
API terms prohibit scraping, bulk messaging, and automated connection requests
Authorization codes live 30 minutes; access tokens last 60 days; programmatic refresh tokens are only available to a limited set of partners
Redirect URLs must be absolute HTTPS URLs; query parameters are ignored and # fragments are not allowed

steps.title: Create a LinkedIn App
steps.description: Go to linkedin.com/developers and click 'Create app'. You must associate the app with a LinkedIn Company Page (you must be an admin of that page). Fill in app name, description, logo, and select 'Legal Agreement'.
warnings: You MUST have a LinkedIn Company Page — create one first if you don't have one
Use your company name, not personal name, for the app

steps.title: Configure OAuth 2.0 Settings
steps.description: In your app's Auth tab, add Authorized Redirect URLs. For Composio: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback. You can also find your Client ID and Client Secret here.

steps.title: Request API Products
steps.description: In your app's Products tab, you'll see available API Products. 'Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect' is available immediately. For other capabilities, click 'Request access' on the relevant product and complete the form explaining your use case.
warnings: Be very specific and honest about your use case — vague descriptions are rejected
LinkedIn reads these carefully; marketing-speak without technical detail causes delays

steps.title: Wait for Product Access Approval
steps.description: LinkedIn reviews product access requests manually. Typical wait: 1–4 weeks. You may receive follow-up questions or be denied with suggestions to apply for a different product. Monitor your email and LinkedIn developer notifications.
warnings: Approval is not guaranteed — LinkedIn denies many requests that don't fit their use-case criteria
There's no appeal process — if denied, you can reapply after addressing their concerns

steps.title: Configure in Composio with Approved Scopes
steps.description: Once products are approved, configure your Composio auth config with the LinkedIn Client ID, Client Secret, and the scopes corresponding to your approved products.
warnings: Requesting scopes beyond your approved products will cause OAuth errors

requirements.account_type: LinkedIn account + Company Page (free; must be Company Page admin)

blockers.title: Company Page Requirement
blockers.description: You cannot create a LinkedIn app without associating it with a LinkedIn Company Page of which you are an admin. Sole proprietors or individual developers must create a Company Page first.
blockers.workaround: Create a LinkedIn Company Page for your project/company before starting app setup. This takes 10–15 minutes.

blockers.title: Approval Not Guaranteed
blockers.description: LinkedIn manually reviews all API product access requests. Requests that don't clearly fit LinkedIn's allowed use cases are denied. Common denials: automated messaging, data harvesting, competitive intelligence.
blockers.workaround: Review LinkedIn's API Terms of Service and permitted use cases before applying. Frame your use case precisely around the specific product capabilities you need.
